holidays.name: National Thrift Shop Day
holidays.description: A day for treasure hunters to dive into secondhand stores, rummage through dusty racks, and score vintage jackets, quirky mugs, and mystery knick-knacks for pocket change.
holidays.origin: National Thrift Shop Day is an unofficial observance that has been celebrated on August 17 in the United States, promoted by thrifting enthusiasts and secondhand retailers to encourage sustainable shopping and reuse.
holidays.funFact: Macklemore's 2012 hit 'Thrift Shop' turned the hunt for a $20 bargain into a global anthem and sent sales of fuzzy fur coats soaring.

holidays.name: National Vanilla Custard Day
holidays.description: A creamy, dreamy day devoted to the silky smooth dessert that sits somewhere between pudding and ice cream. Grab a spoon and indulge in a bowl of golden vanilla goodness.
holidays.origin: This is a food-calendar observance that grew from dessert fans and custard makers. Custard itself dates back to medieval Europe, where it was used as a filling for pies and tarts.
holidays.funFact: The word 'custard' comes from the Middle English 'crustade,' meaning a pie with a crust, because early custards were baked in pastry shells.

holidays.name: Black Cat Appreciation Day
holidays.description: A day for celebrating sleek, shadowy felines and challenging the old superstitions that label them as bad luck. Black cats get extra cuddles, treats, and adoption love.
holidays.origin: Black Cat Appreciation Day is observed on August 17 in the United States and is promoted by animal lovers and shelters to counter the stigma that has made black cats harder to adopt.
holidays.funFact: In some cultures, such as the UK and Japan, black cats are considered lucky, and sailors once kept them on ships to bring good fortune.

holidays.name: Discovery Day (Yukon)
holidays.description: A Canadian territorial holiday in the Yukon celebrating the discovery of gold in the Klondike, which kicked off one of the wildest gold rushes in history. Locals celebrate with parades, festivals, and gold-panning.
holidays.origin: On August 16, 1896, Skookum Jim Mason, Dawson Charlie, and George Carmack found gold on Rabbit Creek, later renamed Bonanza Creek. The Yukon marks the discovery with a holiday on the third Monday of August, which sometimes falls near this date.
holidays.funFact: Tens of thousands of prospectors rushed north, and Dawson City boomed from a tiny settlement into a town of about 30,000 people almost overnight.
